model.name: Data Quality Assessment
model.purpose: Represent one governed, reproducible assessment that qualifies data quality for a declared subject, version, population, purpose and time without treating quality as a universal intrinsic property.
model.scope_statement: Owns assessment identity, version and lifecycle; assessed subject and version bindings; consumer, use case, purpose and fitness criteria; quality framework, categories, dimensions, metrics, rules, thresholds and requirements; plan, population, sample, method, tool and execution references; observations, measurements, violations, scores, uncertainty and purpose-qualified verdicts; evidence, provenance, review, conflicts, annotations, exceptions, issue and remediation references, access, retention, audit and projections. Dataset, data product, contract, schema, pipeline, run, metric registry, issue, remediation, certificate, audit and records masters remain external where authoritative.
in_scope: Assessment identity, subject and version, purpose, audience, quality model, metrics, rules, thresholds, plan, sampling, methods and execution evidence
Observations, results, uncertainty, violations, scores, fitness verdicts, evidence, review, conflicts, exceptions, lifecycle, issue and remediation references, access, records and projections
out_of_scope: Owning Dataset, Data Product, Data Contract, Schema, Pipeline, Run, Issue, Remediation, Certificate, Audit or Records masters
Treating a pass, score, green dashboard, completed run or certificate as proof of universal correctness, completeness, fitness, safety, compliance or absence of harm

Autonomous production-data mutation, contract change, pipeline execution, threshold change, access widening, certification, issue closure, remediation execution, publication or physical records disposition

boundary_notes.distinction: The unified parent signal and incoming candidate relation identify the assessed dataset and version. The assessment owns source-qualified quality definitions and assertions; it does not own dataset identity, contents or lifecycle.
A contract or schema owns agreed structure and obligations. This assessment binds a version and records whether bounded rules were evaluated, not the contract lifecycle itself.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-DAT-005 Data Pipeline and WM-ACT-053 Data Processing Job / Pipeline Run
boundary_notes.distinction: Pipelines own reusable transformations and runs own executions. The assessment references exact runs, inputs and logs while owning the interpretation and verdict for its declared purpose.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Issue, remediation, certificate, audit and records
boundary_notes.distinction: These masters retain independent authority and lifecycles. The assessment stores non-owning references, review evidence, qualified annotations and successor corrections.

boundary_notes.neighbor: DQV, DCAT, PROV, SHACL, JSON Schema, SSN, ISO, UN NQAF, OECD QFS, NIST RDaF, QUDT, OWL-Time and RFC 3339
boundary_notes.distinction: These vocabularies and frameworks have distinct scopes and normative force. Every mapping is version-pinned, profile-qualified and loss-declaring.

composition.purpose: Resolve authoritative definitions, actions, attestations and evidence without changing their ownership.

composition.target: DQV, DCAT 3, PROV-O, SHACL, JSON Schema 2020-12, SSN 2023, ISO/IEC 25012, ISO/IEC 25024, ISO 8000-8, ISO 19157-1, UN NQAF, OECD QFS, NIST RDaF, QUDT 3.1.10, OWL-Time and RFC 3339
composition.purpose: Project version-pinned quality, catalog, provenance, validation, observation, measurement, statistical, research-data, unit and time views with declared loss.

owner_package_requirements: Dimension owner, namespace authority, data governance mandate and accountable data product owner
Authoritative Dataset, Data Product, Data Contract, Schema, Pipeline, Run, Metric, Issue, Remediation, Certificate, Audit and Records registries
Approved quality framework, sampling, measurement, validation, threshold, fitness, security, privacy, access, retention and interoperability profiles
Role, delegation, independence, review, exception, publication, correction, issue, remediation, reassessment and agent-operation policies
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint assessment, version, subject binding, framework, metric, rule, observation, result, verdict, exception, correction and projection IDs; preserve every external master identifier.

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize one assessment by authoritative assessment identifier and issuer namespace, never by subject title, score, date, dashboard URL or report digest alone.
Keep metric definition, rule, measurement activity, observation, result, aggregate score, verdict, certificate, issue and remediation action independently identifiable.
patch_rules: Extensions declare subject type, purpose, framework, dimension, metric, rule, sampling, uncertainty, verdict, privacy, retention and interoperability effects.
Published assessment versions and source evidence are immutable; changes create linked successors with reason, impact and review.
Never silently change subject version, population, purpose, metric formula, unit, threshold, sampling design, weighting, uncertainty, verdict or evidence.
compatibility_rules: Ignore additive fields only when assessment and subject identity, purpose, definitions, values, units, methods, authority, time, uncertainty, access and provenance survive.
Every projection pins standard, vocabulary, schema, quality-framework and mapping versions and declares information loss.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier for each assessment, version, definition, observation, result, verdict or projection, qualified by issuer, namespace and record kind.
Dimension UUID or ULID when neither preceding identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit offset or Z; distinguish phenomenon, reference-period, execution, result, assessed, effective, published, corrected, recorded, ingested and knowledge times whenever they differ.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, record kind, assessment and subject scope, framework and method versions, actor, event and knowledge times, confidentiality marking and provenance.

policies: The assessment owns its governed case, definitions, observations, results, verdicts and version lineage but not Dataset, Data Product, Contract, Schema, Pipeline, Run, Issue, Remediation, Certificate, Audit or Records masters.
Quality is fitness for a declared purpose, stakeholder, subject version, population and time; conflicting assessments may coexist with independent provenance.
Pass, conformance, score, dashboard color, run completion, certificate and remediation status are distinct assertions and never imply universal fitness or absence of harm.

Agents cannot autonomously mutate production data or contracts, execute pipelines, change thresholds, widen access, issue certification, close issues, execute remediation, publish assessments or dispose records without delegated authority.

read: Resolve current head, subject and purpose, framework, metrics, rules, plan, sampling, methods, observations, results, verdicts, evidence, conflicts, issues, remediation references, lifecycle and projection loss under the permitted view.
create: Bind stable assessment identity, issuer, subject and version, purpose, consumer, framework, definitions, plan, method, source authority and initial state before results.
update: Append successor definitions, observations, results, verdicts, reviews, exceptions, corrections and lifecycle assertions with reason, authority, expected revision, event time and knowledge time.
delete: Apply legal hold, reproducibility, privacy, security and adopting-Dimension records policy; withdraw or tombstone only the assessment view without cascading to subject, run, issue, evidence or records masters, and let authoritative systems execute physical disposition.

roles.name: Data product owner
responsibilities: Own assessment purpose, consumer outcomes, risk acceptance and accountable use of quality evidence.

roles.name: Data steward
responsibilities: Own subject semantics, quality framework, requirements, definitions, classifications and retention profiles.

roles.name: Quality analyst and metric author
responsibilities: Define metrics, rules, methods, sampling, thresholds, aggregation, uncertainty and limitations.

roles.name: Assessment operator
responsibilities: Bind inputs, tools, runs, observations, logs and reproducibility evidence without changing authoritative data.

roles.name: Independent reviewer and approval authority
responsibilities: Review scope, methods, evidence, conflicts, verdicts, exceptions and publication decisions within mandate.

roles.name: Subject owner and remediation coordinator
responsibilities: Receive findings, link external issues and actions, and provide retest evidence without rewriting assessments.

roles.name: Privacy, security and records steward
responsibilities: Own protected access, minimization, disclosure, legal hold, retention, disposition, audit and projection policy.

access.default_rule: Deny personal or sensitive source data, proprietary rules or logic, credentials, row-level violations, protected evidence and unpublished verdicts unless a purpose-bound policy permits the minimum necessary view.
exceptions: Declared operations, safety, incident, remediation, privacy, legal, audit or subject-rights access must cite authority, scope, purpose and time limit and must be logged.
audit_requirements: Log actor, agent, role, purpose, assessment and version, subject binding, operation, authority, policy, RFC 3339 time, affected metrics or records, source revision and outcome without unnecessary protected-data duplication.

read_order: Read Dimension data governance, namespace, dataset, product, contract, quality, security, privacy, access, retention, issue, remediation and agent policies.
Read this assessment and linked subject, framework, metric, run, issue, remediation, certificate, evidence, audit and records models before mutation.

coverage.claim: WM-DAT-007 covers one governed data-quality assessment from identity, subject and purpose through quality models, metrics, rules, sampling, methods, observations, results, purpose-qualified verdicts, evidence, conflicts, issues, remediation references, lifecycle, access, records and projections. Domain-specific profiles, restricted standard clauses and independent external review remain deferred.

known_omissions: Claude and Grok each timed out on one bounded attempt; no independent external result was admitted.
The WM-DAT-001 parent signal and candidate incoming COMPOSE relation are not approved frozen composition edges.
Domain-specific metric catalogues, thresholds, sampling methods, uncertainty models, fitness decision rules and certification schemes require separate profiles.
ISO/IEC 25012, ISO/IEC 25024, ISO 8000-8 and ISO 19157-1 are used only from public metadata or preview text; access-restricted clauses were not inferred.
conflicts: Metric definition, rule, measurement activity, observation, result, assessment, verdict, certificate, issue and remediation action are not interchangeable identities.
Conformance to one rule or schema is not proof of fitness for another purpose, population, time, consumer or risk decision.
Missing, unknown, not applicable, not measured, not run, passed, failed, warned, accepted and waived require distinct states.
regional_assumptions: Quality requirements, evidentiary weight, certification, privacy, access, retention and disclosure depend on domain, jurisdiction and organization.
UN and OECD sources are official-statistics profiles; NIST RDaF is a research-data profile and none is universal.
W3C, JSON Schema, ISO, QUDT and RFC sources are versioned profiles and mappings are not assumed binding, lossless or universally applicable.
adversarial_checks: Reject an assessment without stable identity, issuer, subject and version, purpose, consumer, framework, method, reference period, source authority, lifecycle and current head.
Reject silent overwrites of subject scope, population, metric formula, unit, threshold, sampling design, weighting, uncertainty, verdict or evidence.
Reject autonomous production-data mutation, contract change, pipeline execution, threshold change, access expansion, certification, issue closure, remediation execution, publication or disposition.
Reject universal correctness, completeness, fitness, safety or absence of harm inferred only from a pass, score, dashboard color, run completion or certificate.
Reject a projection that collapses metric, rule, observation, result, assessment, verdict, certificate, issue and remediation identities or hides information loss.
